chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:

Indeed, two men disputed before Ali (peace be upon him) regarding a beast of burden. Each claimed it had given birth on his grazing land, and each presented evidence equal in number. So he cast lots between them with two arrows, marking each arrow with a sign for each of them. Then he said: 'O God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and Lord of the Great Throne, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Merciful, the Compassionate, which of them is the owner of the beast and is more entitled to it? So I ask You to cast lots and bring forth his arrow.' Then the arrow of one of them came out, so he ruled in his favor.

key_terms.اخْتَصَمَا: disputed / brought a case before a judge

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali resolve a dispute when two parties presented equal evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the jurisprudential principle of *qur'ah* (casting lots) as a valid judicial tool when evidence (*bayyinah*) is perfectly balanced between two parties. Imam Ali’s specific supplication invokes God as the Knower of the Unseen and Seen, highlighting the Shia scholarly view that *qur'ah* is not mere chance but a divinely guided mechanism (*kashf*) to reveal the truth in ambiguous legal disputes.
